To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we found that weaning increased the proportion of soluble zinc in the gastrointestinal tract, that the proportion of soluble iron was higher for unweaned pigs compared with weaned pigs, and that weaned pigs fed high doses of zinc showed higher soluble copper in the gastrointestinal tract compared with weaned and unweaned pigs.

we found a 3 to 10 fold increased concentration of Zn in the GIT of weaned pigs treated with 2 g/kg of ZnO compared to unweaning and control weaned pigs and that this Zn was mainly present in the soluble form.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of action of high doses of ZnO used to treat diarrhea and with the optimization of its use.
the study of the effect of ZnO supplementation on the solubilization and absorption of Zn, Fe, Cu in weaning pigs.
the effect of ZnO supplementation on the solubilization and absorption of Zn, Fe, Cu, and other minerals in the GIT of weaned pigs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Zn, Fe, Cu are differently affected along the GIT by weaning and ZnO treatment.
ZnO supplementation in the diet increases the concentration of Zn and Cu in the soluble fraction of the GIT content of weaned pigs.

the ZnO treatment in the diet of weaned pigs increased the Zn concentration in the GIT content, especially in the soluble fraction, and this increase was not related to the proportion of soluble fraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
weaning is associated with an increase of soluble Zn and Fe and a decrease of Cu along the GIT.
Zn is more soluble in weaned pigs compared to unweaning ones and that this difference is not affected by the high dose of ZnO.
weaning is an important factor for the absorption of Zn and Fe, and ZnO supplementation is an important factor in the solubilization of Zn and Cu.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ZnO treatment increases the solubilized fraction of Zn and Cu in distal parts (cecum and proximal colon) of the GIT of weaned pigs, and this increase in solubilized fractions of Cu is higher than the one of Zn.

the amount of solubilizated Zn, the relation with Fe and Cu and the concentration of Zn, Fe, Cu along the GIT of piglets weaning with or without high doses of ZnO compared to unweaning littermates are key data to understand the mechanism of action of this compound.
weaning increases the amount of zinc, iron and copper that are soluble in the gut.
